raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes the Model Runner V1 side of #60357: entries requested through `logprob_token_ids` came back with their position in the request list as `rank` instead of their vocab rank. The Rust engine-core client also learns to decode the per-entry ranks this now sends. The V2 side is covered by #36746 (see Details).

## Claims

- On Model Runner V1, every `logprob_token_ids` entry reports its vocab rank, using the `>=` definition vLLM already uses for the sampled token. Untied tokens match `logprobs=-1` exactly; tied ones report the end of their tie group.
- The Rust frontend decodes the per-entry ranks. Without that, a gRPC request with a `token_ids` candidate selector on a V1 engine would fail with `new_logprobs.token_ranks: expected rank-1 array, got rank 2`.
- The top-k and `logprobs=-1` paths are untouched, and typical label lists (2 to 10 ids) cost nothing measurable.

## Validation

GPU runs on 1x H100 MIG 1g.12gb (CUDA 13.2), Rust checks on macOS; branch rebased on `df417f780a`.

**Repro from #60357** (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, greedy, one token, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`):

| token | rank before | rank after | `logprobs=-1` rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12095 `" Paris"` (sampled) | 5 | 1 | 1 |
| 279 `" the"` | 1 | 3 | 3 |
| 264 `" a"` | 2 | 9 | 9 |
| 13 `"."` | 3 | 121 | 115 (7 tokens tied) |
| 11 `","` | 4 | 30 | 28 (3 tokens tied) |

Logprob values are identical before and after; only `rank` changes. The repro also runs clean with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on both runners.

**Tests.** The three new tests fail before this change (`rank 3, expected within [1, 1]` for the greedy token on both runners).

```
pytest tests/test_logprobs.py tests/v1/sample/test_sampler.py \
  "tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_logprob_token_ids_ranks"
  -> 47 passed, 1 xfailed (the V2 case, see Details)
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_logprob_token_ids.py   -> 9 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py -k logprob   -> 4 passed
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -k "not spec_decode and not large_batch"   -> 42 passed, 1 xfailed (+3, see notes)
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py   -> 40 passed (+7, see notes)

# in rust/
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                  -> clean
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  -> clean
cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client --all-features --locked              -> 128 passed
```

<details>
<summary>Local environment notes</summary>

- Gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B(-Instruct)` was swapped for the `unsloth/` mirrors locally. The 7 `test_stop_token` cases in `test_output_processor.py` assert the `meta-llama/` model id and fail the same way on `main` with the mirror.
- On the 12 GB MIG slice, 3 prompt-logprob tests in `tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py` only fit in a fresh process (earlier engines in the module hold memory); they pass when run on their own.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 2019 passed. The 6 failures (`vllm-chat` audio/roundtrip, `vllm-text` qwen defaults) come from HF hub downloads and tokenizer-config drift on my machine; the same tests fail on `main` too.

</details>

**Python to Rust wire check.** I encoded `EngineCoreOutputs` built from the real V1 `Sampler.gather_specific_token_logprobs` output with `MsgpackEncoder`, plus a top-k request in the same frame, and decoded the bytes with the Rust client. This branch decodes ranks `[1, 5, 2, 4]` for the `logprob_token_ids` request and leaves the top-k request as before; `main`'s decoder rejects the frame with the rank-1 error above.

**With #36746 applied on top** (its `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/*` files), `test_logprob_token_ids_ranks` passes on both runners: 1 passed, 1 xpassed.

**Sampler cost.** `Sampler.gather_specific_token_logprobs`, 152k vocab, mean of 20 iterations after warm-up, `main` vs this PR:

| batch | 2 ids | 10 ids | 128 ids (max) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.28 vs 0.27 ms | 0.28 vs 0.26 ms | 0.29 vs 0.28 ms |
| 32 | 0.71 vs 0.68 ms | 0.71 vs 0.70 ms | 0.91 vs 2.07 ms |
| 128 | 1.98 vs 1.95 ms | 2.02 vs 2.04 ms | 2.79 vs 8.12 ms |

Only requests that set `logprob_token_ids` reach this code. No model eval: sampled tokens and logprob values are unchanged, only the `rank` metadata is.

## Details

**Root cause.** Only the sampled token got a real rank: `selected_token_ranks` is one value per position. `append_logprobs_for_next_position` then gave the remaining entries `1..k`, which is right for the top-k path because those columns are sorted, but `logprob_token_ids` columns are in request order. When the sampled token was also in the list, its real rank was overwritten by its list position in the per-position dict.

**Change.**
- `Sampler.gather_specific_token_logprobs` ranks every gathered column with `batched_count_greater_than_per_value`, a compiled reduction next to `batched_count_greater_than`. It never materializes the `[batch, ids, vocab]` comparison, and the batch and column dims are marked unbacked so a new list length doesn't recompile. In this mode `selected_token_ranks` is `[num_positions, max_num_logprobs + 1]`.
- `append_logprobs_for_next_position` accepts a rank per entry; the scalar path is unchanged.
- Rust: `token_ranks` may be 1-D or 2-D, and 2-D ranks are used as-is.

A per-column loop over the existing helper was my first version; at batch 128 with 128 ids the call took 23.4 ms instead of 2.8 ms, so I compared it against sort + `searchsorted` and a hand-written Triton kernel. The single compiled reduction was the best overall; sorting only won at the very largest size.

**Why V1.** V1 is still selected for some ROCm architectures, without Triton, and for features MRV2 doesn't support yet (sequence parallelism, prefill context parallelism, several spec-decode methods), so scoring there still returns wrong ranks. MRV2 has the same bug.

**Relation to #36746** (cc @mvanhorn). It already moves V2 to per-entry 2-D ranks while de-duplicating `top_logprobs`, but keeps the V1 sampler 1-D, so this isn't a duplicate. I used the same representation (2-D `selected_token_ranks`, a rank list in `append_logprobs_for_next_position`, 1-D or 2-D `token_ranks` in Rust) so the two compose: whichever lands second will hit textual conflicts in those spots but no design change. The V2 case of the new end-to-end test is `xfail` (non-strict) until #36746 lands.

**Ties.** Ranks keep the existing `>=` definition, which also keeps NaN at rank 0 as the Rust decoder documents. `logprobs=-1` numbers tied tokens sequentially, so the two modes can differ within a tie group; the test accepts any position inside the group.

**Out of scope.** Under speculative decoding `logprob_token_ids` currently returns almost no logprobs; that's #42592 / #44727.

---

+        params = []
+        for output in full:

+            ids = [by_rank[i] for i in (99, 9, 0, 29)]
+            params.append(
+                SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=3, logprob_token_ids=ids)
+            )
+        selected = runner.llm.generate(example_prompts, params)
+
+    for full_output, selected_output in zip(full, selected):
+        full_completion = full_output.outputs[0]
+        completion = selected_output.outputs[0]
+        assert completion.token_ids == full_completion.token_ids
+        for full_pos, pos in zip(full_completion.logprobs, completion.logprobs):
+            vocab_logprobs = np.array([lp.logprob for lp in full_pos.values()])

+                # tie may land anywhere in its run of equal logprobs.

+                worst = int((vocab_logprobs >= ref).sum())

+                    f"token {token_id}: rank {logprob.rank}, "
+                    f"expected within [{best}, {worst}]"
+                )
